main_body: Round stone well curb with a dark water opening, topped by a thin wooden crossbeam on two posts
top_band: Light grey-green stone rim ring, rows ~14-17 at the back, then the dark blue water ellipse rows ~17-21, then the front rim rows ~21-23
evidence: Reading down the centre column: the lightest grey rim at rows 14-16, the dark navy water ellipse with a highlight at rows 17-21, a lighter front rim at about row 22, then the darker stone-block front face to row 31. The opening reads as an ellipse with visible water, so the horizontal surface is clearly seen from above, matching the well reference. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The stone has about 4 teal-grey steps with blocks shaded individually and the water has a small highlight. The outlines are tinted dark teal and brown rather than black. The wooden beam and posts are almost flat orange with only 2-3 tones and no grain, which leaves large flat fills. The beam is a thin plain bar next to the reference's tiled, shaded roof. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the Beodeul well, so it falls short of the reference bar.
